speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the feeding difficulties and abdominal distension first started, and if the baby is passing stool regularly?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby had any vomiting, and if so, is it green or yellow? Also, is he passing any gas or stool at all?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify if the baby is passing any gas or stool, as the absence of both could indicate a blockage. Also, has there been any blood in the stool, and can you describe the texture of any stool that has been passed? Finally, was there any meconium passed within the first 48 hours after birth?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray. The absence of stool or gas combined with worsening distension suggests a possible intestinal obstruction like Hirschsprung disease or a meconium plug, so I need to see the bowel gas pattern immediately.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray shows dilated bowel segments with an absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel with no rectal gas strongly suggest Hirschsprung disease, so I need to confirm this. REQUEST TEST: Rectal Suction Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The requested Rectal Suction Biopsy results are not available in the provided data. However, the existing Barium Enema findings show a transition zone in the distal colon, which is compatible with Hirschsprung disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The barium enema showing a transition zone in the distal colon confirms the diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease.
